extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards and criteria governing appeals to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (jurisdiction transfer, replies, remands, new grounds of rejection, oral hearings, and post-decision procedures) under relevant 37 CFR provisions and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization of rejections under 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2) for amendments under 37 CFR 1.116
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 proposes to combine limitations of previously rejected claims (e.g., combine claims 1 and 2 into a new claim), 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2) would authorize a rejection in the examiner's answer under 35 U.S.C. 103 on the basis of Reference A in view of Reference B, provided the applicant was advised that this rejection would be applied to the new/ amended claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: combining claim 1 and 2 allows A in view of B rejection if that rejection was advised; combining claim 1 and 3 allows A in view of C rejection if advised. However, combining limitations of claims 1, 2, and 3 into a single new claim does NOT authorize a rejection of that new claim under A in view of B and C together even if the applicant was advised; such an amendment may raise a new issue and may be refused entry. Emphasizes that 1.193(a)(2) controls what rejections may be applied in an examiner's answer, but does not change 1.116 practice on whether an amendment is entitled to entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between entitlement to entry (37 CFR 1.116) and rejection authorization (37 CFR 1.193(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amended 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2) authorizes what rejections a claim added or amended in an amendment under 37 CFR 1.116 may be subject to in an examiner's answer. The provisions of 37 CFR 1.116 still control whether an amendment under 1.116 is entitled to entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if 1.193(a)(2) would authorize a rejection in an examiner's answer of a claim sought to be added or amended, that fact has no effect on whether the amendment is entitled to entry. The 1.116 entry provisions remain the gating consideration; 1.193(a)(2) only governs later rejections in the examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of a new prior art reference in examiner's answer generally constitutes a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A new prior art reference cited for the first time in an examiner's answer generally will constitute a new ground of rejection and, if necessary to support a rejection, must be included in the statement of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if cited to support the rejection in a minor capacity, the new reference should be positively included in the statement of rejection (In re Hoch). Exception: if the newly cited reference is added merely as evidence of a prior well-known statement made by the examiner, citation of the reference in the examiner's answer would not constitute a new ground of rejection within the meaning of 37 CFR 1.192(a)(2). See also MPEP § 2144.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of allegation of impermissible new ground if not timely raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Any allegation that an examiner's answer contains an impermissible new ground of rejection is waived if not timely raised by way of a petition under 37 CFR 1.181(a); specifically, 37 CFR 1.181(f) governs timeliness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must timely file the appropriate petition to preserve the objection to a new ground in an examiner's answer; failure to timely petition constitutes waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution after appeal (authority and conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may, with supervisory patent examiner approval, reopen prosecution to enter a new ground of rejection after appellant's brief or reply brief has been filed. The Office action containing a new ground may be made final if (A) necessitated by amendment, or (B) based on information presented in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) where no certification was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 12.81 may be used to reopen prosecution. When prosecution is reopened, appellant must either file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111/1.113 (depending on finality) or request reinstatement of the appeal. If reinstating the appeal, a supplemental appeal brief is required but no new amendments, affidavits (37 CFR 1.130–1.132) or other evidence are permitted. The supplemental brief must comply with 37 CFR 1.192(c) and may incorporate by reference prior brief portions; arguments need only address the new ground(s) of rejection but should identify still-relevant previously raised issues. If the examiner does not consider the supplemental brief complies, appellant should be given a one-month opportunity to file an amended supplemental brief under 37 CFR 1.192(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Options to appellant after prosecution is reopened to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: After reopening of prosecution, to avoid abandonment appellant must either (A) file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 (if non-final) or 37 CFR 1.113 (if final) or (B) request reinstatement of the appeal accompanied by a supplemental appeal brief (no new amendments/evidence permitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reinstatement is requested, the original fees (notice of appeal, appeal brief, request for oral hearing) may be applied to a later appeal on the same application. A supplemental appeal brief may incorporate by reference previously-filed material and should address new grounds raised in the reopening action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief filing and examiner's obligations (37 CFR 1.193(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a reply brief as a matter of right within two months from the mailing date of the examiner's answer. The primary examiner must either acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief or withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution to respond to the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time governed by 37 CFR 1.136(b) or 1.550(c). A supplemental examiner's answer is not permitted unless remanded by the Board. Amendments, affidavits, or other evidence must be submitted in papers separate from the reply brief; a paper containing an amendment is not a reply brief merely by characterization and will not be entitled to entry simply for being called a reply brief. Acknowledgment of receipt/entry (form paragraph 12.47) indicates no further examiner response deemed necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request timing, fee, and usage (37 CFR 1.194)
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only when appellant considers it necessary or desirable. If desired, appellant must file a written request in a separate paper with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(d) within two months from the date of the examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no timely request/fee, the appeal will be assigned and decided on the briefs. If requested and fee submitted, a hearing day is set and oral argument is generally limited to 20 minutes for appellant and 15 minutes for the primary examiner (unless otherwise ordered). Appellant may request additional time in advance; final decision rests with senior panel member. Telephone argument requests are possible (appellant bears cost). Post-confirmation failure to appear results in decision on brief; postponements discouraged and require convincing reasons. Examiner participation may be requested by examiner via form paragraph 12.63 or appropriate acknowledgment when timing differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner participation in oral hearing and time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant requests an oral hearing and submits the fee, the primary examiner may present oral argument if considered desirable by either the primary examiner or the Board. At hearing, after appellant's presentation, the examiner is allowed 15 minutes to reply and present a statement of position; appellant may use unused time for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner requests to present argument, the request must be included in the examiner's answer as the last paragraph (form paragraph 12.63). The application file will be delivered to the examiner at least two weeks before the hearing; the file must be returned to the Board at least two working days before the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of jurisdiction to the Board and items considered after transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The application file and jurisdiction normally transfer to the Board: (A) after two months from the examiner's answer plus mail time if no reply brief filed; (B) after a supplemental examiner's answer pursuant to remand; or (C) after examiner notifies appellant that reply brief has been entered and considered (e.g., PTOL-90 with form paragraph 12.47).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment, affidavit, or other paper relating to the appeal filed after transfer of jurisdiction but before Board decision may be considered by the examiner only if the case is remanded by the Board for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divided jurisdiction when appeal taken from some claims only
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appeal is taken from the second or final rejection only of one or more claims presented for provoking an interference, jurisdiction of the rest of the case remains with the examiner and prosecution of the remaining claims may proceed as though the entire case was under the examiner's jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, where the examiner certifies no conflict of subject matter and the administrative patent judge approves, an appeal may proceed concurrently with an interference. See MPEP § 2315.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board order requiring appellant to identify real party in interest or related cases (compliance order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require the appellant to explicitly name the real party in interest or explicitly identify any related cases if not set out in the brief; an order for compliance will set a one-month period for reply under 37 CFR 1.192(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions only under 37 CFR 1.136(b). A simple paper identifying the real party in interest or stating that appellant is the real party suffices; failure to timely respond may result in dismissal of the appeal. An entire new brief need not be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand by Board: grounds and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may remand a case to the examiner for further consideration when necessary (e.g., fuller description of claimed invention, statement of mode of operation for a machine, further explanation of pertinence of references, selection of preferred ground where rejections are cumulative, further search, or to consider amendment/affidavit/declaration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On remand the examiner may prepare a supplemental examiner's answer using form paragraph 12.80. Supervisory Patent Examiner should approve and the Board should be notified whenever a remanded application is withdrawn from appeal. The Board may also remand to have the examiner prepare a supplemental answer in response to a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits or declarations filed after appeal (37 CFR 1.195)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits, declarations, or exhibits submitted after the case has been appealed will not be admitted without a showing of good and sufficient reasons why they were not earlier presented; affidavits filed after notice of appeal but before jurisdiction passes to the Board may be considered for entry only if the appellant makes the necessary showing under 37 CFR 1.195.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If affidavits/declarations are filed after the application has been forwarded to the Board, the examiner lacks authority to consider them absent a remand. On remand the examiner will consider the affidavit/declaration only if accompanied by the required showing; if delay is satisfactorily explained the examiner will admit and consider the merits. The Board does not customarily remand affidavits/declarations offered for rehearing where no rejection under 37 CFR 1.196(b) is involved; such papers are then considered only as arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may require appellant to address matters for reasoned decision (37 CFR 1.196(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require appellant to address any matter deemed appropriate for a reasoned decision on the pending appeal (e.g., applicability of particular case law or prior art not previously identified). The appellant will be given a non-extendable time period to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond within the time set will result in dismissal of the appeal. The making of such a requirement is discretionary and does not affect the Board's authority to remand the case to the examiner where appropriate. After reply to a requirement, remand may still be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision outcomes and the effect of new grounds of rejection (37 CFR 1.196 & 1.197)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may affirm, reverse, or remand the examiner's decision in whole or in part; it may include a new ground of rejection in its decision. A new ground of rejection in the Board's decision is not final for purposes of judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board makes a new ground under 1.196(b), appellant has two months to: (1) submit appropriate amendments or showings of facts and have the matter reconsidered by the examiner (resulting in remand), or (2) request rehearing under 1.197(b) on the same record, addressing the new ground with particularity. The new ground is binding on the examiner unless an amendment or showing not previously of record overcomes it (in examiner's opinion). The request for rehearing must state with particularity the points believed misapprehended or overlooked. Rehearing decision is final for judicial review except as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement that a claim may be allowed in amended form by the Board (37 CFR 1.196(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board's decision includes an explicit statement that a claim may be allowed in amended form, appellant has the right to amend in conformity with such statement, and that statement shall be binding on the examiner in the absence of new references or grounds of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The making of such a statement is discretionary with the Board. Absent an express statement, a remark that a feature does not appear in a claim is not to be taken as an allowance that the claim will be allowed if that feature is supplied by amendment. Amendment in conformity with a 1.196(c) statement may be exercised only within the period allowed for seeking court review under 37 CFR 1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and availability of Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions of the Board may be published at the discretion of the Commissioner. A decision in a pending or abandoned application will be published in accordance with 37 CFR 1.14(d). Decisions open to the public are made available electronically on the USPTO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to publish a decision should be referred to the Office of the Solicitor. Publication is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure following Board decision and request for rehearing (37 CFR 1.197)
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Board, the application will be returned to the examiner for such further action as required to carry the decision into effect. A request for rehearing by the Board of a rejection under 1.196(b) must be filed within two months from the date of the decision (extensions per 1.196(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By requesting rehearing in this manner, the appellant waives the right to further prosecution before the examiner. If the Board's decision also includes an affirmance of the examiner's rejection, a request for rehearing of that affirmance should be filed in a separate paper to facilitate consideration.
